entry.title: Add a fourth polite form to two auxiliary drills
entry.content:
Add a fourth polite form to two auxiliary drills

n3-03 (〜ようになる) and n3-31 (〜てみる) only exposed 3 and 2 forms to the
Auxiliary Verbs drill. Both take a natural polite past-negative —
〜ようになりませんでした ("did not become able to read X"), 〜てみませんでした
("did not try eating X") — so add it. The other 2-form auxiliaries stay
as they are: their remaining forms ("〜ておきません", "〜てしまいません") are
the ones the reviewed comments call unnatural.

entry.title: Give the Adverbs grammar drill an N2 pattern
entry.content:
Give the Adverbs grammar drill an N2 pattern

The Adverbs focus died above N3 — every N2/N1 pattern is clause-level with
no slot a manner adverb fits. n2-30 (〜とはいえ) is the exception: its
conceded quality is an adjective, so it takes a degree adverb the same
way n4-30 does. Add an always-on degree-adverb slot there (最も dropped —
"it is most cheap" doesn't read) and extend HERO_FOCUS_LEVELS.adverb to
N2. N1 still has none and is left as-is.

audit:hero-focus: N2 adverb 0 → 1 pattern, reach 14. Drift, empty-stream
and slot-scope checks pass; audit:sentences unchanged.

entry.title: Persist profile/daily-goal writes outside the setState updater
entry.content:
Persist profile/daily-goal writes outside the setState updater

updateProfile and toggleGoal/completeGoal ran their persistence side
effect — which dispatches a DOM event that other useUserProfile /
useDailyGoals subscribers react to with setState — inside the functional
setState updater. React runs those updaters during the render phase, so
saving the name on the redesigned Profile page fired a setState on the
still-mounted UserProfileMenu mid-render ("Cannot update a component
while rendering a different component").

Merge the partial against a ref instead and move setState + save into the
caller's event-handler scope, where the cross-component sync is fine.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Square the furi/EN toggles outside a control-group
entry.content:
Square the furi/EN toggles outside a control-group

.app-display-toggle sets a 0.55rem radius, but .control-chip's pill radius
is defined later in the file and wins at equal specificity, so a furi/EN
button only looked square where a .control-group-* wrapper bumped the
specificity (dashboard, KanjiLab, FocusedVocabPractice). The standalone
ふり toggles in ChoiceDrill and SentenceBuilder fell back to the pill.
Pin the square shape to .control-chip.app-display-toggle so it matches the
dashboard everywhere.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

entry.title: Rotate the adjective, not just its ending, in grammar mode (n5-17)
entry.content:
Rotate the adjective, not just its ending, in grammar mode (n5-17)

The Grammar-mode adjective drill held one sentence still and rotated a
part of speech, but on n5-17 (Object が Adjective) the adjective slot was
picked off a fixed seed and never consulted slotSeeds/avoidWords, so the
drill could only toggle the predicate ending on a single adjective —
面白いです → 面白くないです → 面白かったです and back. Reach 5, and a
learner exhausts it in one screen.

Extract the per-adjective noun pool into objectPoolFor() and, on a drill
rotation, hold the noun fixed and swap in another adjective the same noun
legitimately takes — every candidate is one whose own reviewed pool
already contains this noun, stays within the base adjective's descriptive
family, and excludes the curated-allow-list and abstract-evaluation
adjectives whose pairings don't generalise across a loose category match.

Base-path generation is unchanged (audit:sentences identical: 13493/457).
audit:hero-focus: N5 adjective reach 5 → 14, shown 5 → 13; all-levels
median reach 6 → 14. Drift and empty-stream checks still pass.

entry.title: Redesign the Quest hub as a single tappable path instead of a busy da…
entry.content:
Redesign the Quest hub as a single tappable path instead of a busy dashboard

Replaces the always-expanded quest-focus panel (full description, meta
row, five-row step list, guardian aside) plus the separate per-arc
journey-road cards with one continuous path of all twelve stops. Tapping
an open stop reveals a bottom quest sheet with the patron's request,
guardian, reward, and step progress — detail that used to load in front
of every visit now shows up only when asked for.

Each quest gains a patron: a villager, shopkeeper, officer, teacher,
merchant, or lord who is the one actually asking for the quest, giving
the campaign's yōkai-stole-the-seals premise a face and a voice per stop
instead of one abstract goal.

Small motion stands in for "movement" along the path: the current stop
pulses, a just-cleared stop pops, and the stop it unlocks pings a beat
later — the study screens are still where the walking happens.

entry.title: Namespace the home quest card CSS and settle the scene
entry.content:
Namespace the home quest card CSS and settle the scene

Rename the card's classes to a home-quest- prefix so they stop colliding
with the existing .dashboard-quest-button / -mark rules and a parallel
katana-themed draft that also lives under .dashboard-quest-* — that
collision was forcing the scene layer to static and blowing the card up
to ~670px tall.

Also: fade the torii/road still in from the left and drop it to 0.4
opacity, inset the last node so its bead clears the card edge, and seat
the bead on the node instead of floating above it.
